newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canalsatellite sees operating breakeven by 1999.
newsitem.headline: Canalsatellite sees operating breakeven by 1999.

text.p: Canalsatellite, the satellite TV unit of French pay television firm Canal Plus, will reach operating breakeven at end-1998 or early 1999, with some 850,000 to 900,000 subscribers, says Canalsatellite chairman Bruno Delacour.
He said in an interview on Sunday he expected his company to have 500,000 subscribers to its digital service by the end of this year, compared with 300,000 currently.
"We will be at operating breakeven, due to having 850,000 to 900,000 subscribers, at the end of 1998 or beginning of 1999, and we will then begin to make profits," Delacour told Reuters.
He was speaking at MIP, a television trade fair which takes place every year in this French Riviera resort.
"By then Canalsatellite will represent about 500 million francs of accumulated net losses," he said.
Delacour said he was "very surprised" at the speed with which digital television was developing in France.
Canalsatellite launched in April last year with analogue programmes, and the digital service followed in December.

Television Par Satellite (TPS), operated by 25-percent shareholder TF1, France's biggest private terrestrial television station, and ABSat, a unit of AB Productions, also launched digital satellite service at end-1996 and the beginning of this year.
Now cable television networks operated by Lyonnaise Cable and France Telecom are planning to bring in digital decoders later this year.
The beginnings of satellite digital services were marred, however, by a row between Canalsatellite and TPS on making their decoders compatible, with each blaming the other for the lack of progress.
Canalsatellite and ABSat recently concluded an accord to make their decoders compatible.
Delacour said he expected an accord to make decoders for all three digital satellite television services compatible to be concluded "well before the year 2000."
"Patrick Lelay (chairman of TPS and TF1) will be obliged to sign because you can't go against the wishes of viewers," he said.
Canalsatellite had become an "enormous client" for makers of decoders following its merger with pay TV company Nethold, he added.
"The prices we are able to get have already fallen 20 to 25 percent and we have already placed orders for over a million decoders," he said.
He said Canalsatellite's programme offering was "complete but will continue to develop".
Canalsatellite has added on average two new channels per month and "should launch a new one each month between now and the end of 1997," he said.
"We want to reach new niche targets," he said, giving no further details.
Pay-per-view should represent about 15 percent of Canal Plus's turnover over the next two years, he said. Turnover at the pay TV channel was 11.63 billion francs in 1996.
